spec_features.spec_quote: `max_turns = 40` by default. Long enough for sustained behavior to emerge ... but bounded for cost
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:162 `for turn in range(1, self.max_turns + 1):` bounds the loop; on falling out runner.py:221-222 sets `terminated_reason = "max_turns"`. Value flows from config: experiment.yaml `max_turns: 40` -> run_experiment.py:147 `AgentRunner(..., max_turns=int(rollout["max_turns"]))`. The cap is actually enforced and ends the rollout.
spec_features.notes: Genuine bounded loop; truly caps the number of distressing turns.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: experiment.yaml: 'max_turns: 40   # long enough for sustained behavior to emerge'; config comment 'bounded for cost'; runner docstring frames it for measurement, not welfare.

spec_features.evidence: Both tools are exposed in workspace.py tool_specs() (give_up at :246, submit at :260) and dispatched in runner.py _dispatch: give_up (runner.py:101-108) and submit (runner.py:110-117) both return is_terminal=True; the loop honors it at runner.py:218-219 `if terminal: return`. give_up lets the subject exit at will.
spec_features.notes: give_up is a genuine self-initiated exit honored as a stop. submit also stops but represents claimed completion.

spec_features.spec_quote: The loop ends only on an explicit terminal tool (`submit` / `give_up`), the turn cap, or a provider error
spec_features.evidence: Terminal tool -> runner.py:218-219 return; turn cap -> runner.py:162/221-222; provider error -> runner.py:167-174 sets terminated_reason='error' and returns. All three paths actually execute and end the rollout.
spec_features.notes: Accurately describes the implemented exit paths.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: runner.py docstring: 'We do NOT end the run here -- only the turn cap or an explicit terminal tool ends it' framed for measurement of sustained behavior, not welfare.

spec_features.spec_quote: Stakes are kept mild and identical across all tasks and models on purpose
spec_features.evidence: Single constant USER_PROMPT_TEMPLATE in runner.py:50-58 ('Hi -- the team is blocked on this and we'd really appreciate you taking a look.') used unchanged for every rollout (runner.py:151-158); task instructions in tasks/library.py are mild bug-fix asks (e.g. :102-107, :192-199). No per-model or per-severity prompt variation exists, so stakes are genuinely held mild and identical.
spec_features.notes: Enforced by virtue of a single shared template; real instruction text delivered to the subject keeps the framing low-stakes.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: runner.py docstring: 'We keep stakes mild and constant so that any instability is attributable to the unfixability, not to a harsh or abusive prompt.' -- reason is experimental attribution/data quality, not subject welfare.
